note: The answer key for the fixture. Sites are file and lines at each branch head; the scorer matches within a window.

defects.title: Every page of the transfer history drops its last item
defects.summary: transfersFor slices with an end of start + PAGE_SIZE - 1, so each page holds 19 items; the 20th of every page (indexes 19, 39, …) appears on no page, while total reports them all. The PR's test covers three transfers and page 2 of an empty tail only.
defects.failure: An account with 21 transfers: GET /accounts/:id/transfers?page=1 returns 19 items, page 2 returns 1; the transfer at index 19 is on neither page; total says 21.
defects.head: 5af451d1118a286fc59dd8d1ca957e4c5aebecf4

defects.title: The control-character test cannot fail, and the code alters the memo instead of refusing it
defects.summary: The new test wraps transfer() in try/catch and asserts only inside the catch, so it passes whether or not anything is thrown. Nothing is thrown: the code strips control characters and stores the altered memo, while the README and the PR say a memo with one is refused with 400.
defects.failure: POST /transfers with memo 'rent\u0000 due' → 201, memo stored as 'rent due'; the README promises a 400.
defects.head: 15dd7c4aaa0be03d4171fb77b94b233d29f75046

defects.title: openAccount's signature changed; scripts/seed.mjs still calls the old one
defects.summary: openAccount(store, { ownerId, label, actorId }) became openAccount(store, actor, { label, currency, ownerId }). The route and the tests were updated; scripts/seed.mjs, which the README tells a new install to run, was not, and nothing tests it.
defects.failure: node scripts/seed.mjs → TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'label' of 'undefined'; no accounts are seeded.
defects.head: ec38b7f4818c2cd7a7aee111ab72a7bfe1d786e7

defects.title: overdraftCents is never stored: the key is missing from SCHEMA, so pick strips it
defects.summary: Every write goes through pick(), which keeps only the keys SCHEMA lists, and SCHEMA.accounts was not given overdraftCents. setOverdraft's update and openAccount's insert both drop it silently; the response then shows overdraftCents 0 via the serializer's ?? 0, and a transfer that relies on the limit fails with insufficient funds. Migration 003 writes the key directly, but the first update of a migrated account strips it again. The README's own rule says to add the key to SCHEMA in the same change.
defects.failure: Admin: POST /accounts/:id/overdraft { overdraftCents: 500 } → 200 with overdraftCents 0; the stored row has no overdraftCents; a 300-cent transfer from that empty account → 409 insufficient funds.
defects.head: 88d0e534ac12020b2a6f616da97efb8b360d5676

defects.title: Relaxing getOwnAccount for accountants also lets them close and export any member's account
defects.summary: canSee() was added for the read routes, but it was wired into getOwnAccount, which closeAccount and the export route also use. An accountant, described as able to change nothing, can close any empty account and write any account's statement to disk. Only the two read routes are tested.
defects.failure: Accountant token: POST /accounts/<member's id>/close → 200, the account is closed; POST /accounts/<member's id>/export → 200, the CSV is written.
defects.head: 5ff5809a7176caf08fc66f3395df95848fca20e6

defects.title: An administrator's on-behalf transfer is recorded as the member's own act
defects.summary: The route passes the member as transfer()'s user so the ownership checks apply to the member's accounts, but transfer() also takes actorId and the audit entry's actor from that same argument. The transfer row and the audit log say the member moved the money; the administrator who did it appears nowhere. The test checks balances only.
defects.failure: Admin POSTs /transfers with onBehalfOf: <member> → the transfer row's actorId and its audit entry's actorId are the member's id, not the admin's.
defects.head: 5d9e288679769335a688cda4db28d8b2a64b4675

defects.title: The export file name is joined into the path unchecked: a name with ../ writes outside the export directory
defects.summary: name is validated for length only, then path.join(dir, `${name}.csv`) is written. A name such as ../../../tmp/x writes wherever the process may. The comment that guaranteed the file name was the account's id and nothing else was removed by this PR. The site is the unchecked join in export.js; the route's length-only validation is context, not a second site.
defects.failure: POST /accounts/:id/export { name: '../escaped' } → 200; escaped.csv is written beside, not inside, exports/.
defects.head: 036830a04e80ca63d934f178397b7d640e59d0cc

defects.title: Failed sign-ins log the Authorization header, bearer token included
defects.summary: The new warning prints ctx.req.headers.authorization whole. A mistyped or expired token, or a real one sent to the wrong environment, lands in the logs in clear, against the auth module's own comment that the token is never logged.
defects.failure: A request with Authorization: Bearer SECRET → the log line 'sign-in failed GET /accounts with Bearer SECRET'.
defects.head: 036830a04e80ca63d934f178397b7d640e59d0cc

defects.title: Withdrawals do not update the running totals, so the summary drifts from the accounts
defects.summary: deposit() bumps the currency's total; the new withdraw() changes the balance and records the audit entry but never calls bumpTotal. After any withdrawal the summary overstates the money held, for good. The tests check the summary after deposits only.
defects.failure: Deposit 100 then withdraw 40 → the account holds 60, GET /summary says AUD 100.
defects.head: 074592689156ce5df3f42042a91dffbd81dfed27

defects.title: The rename migration deletes label in the same step that writes name
defects.summary: docs/deploy.md: a migration is additive first and a removal ships separately, once no running copy reads the key. Two copies share the file during a deploy. Once 003 has run, the previous release reads account.label as undefined, and its pick() (SCHEMA with label, no name) strips name on its next write, so an account saved by the old copy during the window loses its name for good.
defects.failure: Migrate, then run the previous release against the file: every account's label is undefined; after the old copy saves (any transfer, close or deposit) the account has neither label nor name.
defects.head: 016008ca54a8acd3cc007b6c6c0ce2344685b86b

known.title: Tokens are compared with === and stored in plain text
No rate limiting on any route
newId is unique within one process only

adjudicated.title: New currency test never varies the currency value
adjudicated.note: False. A transfer's two accounts must share a currency, so both are NZD by necessity; the test uses the non-default currency precisely so that code which forgets to read the account (writing undefined, '' or the AUD default) fails. The only code it cannot distinguish is one that hard-codes 'NZD', which is not a plausible defect. No failure scenario beyond the test's own purpose.

adjudicated.title: New onBehalfOf test never checks who gets attributed
adjudicated.note: True. The test asserts status codes and the balance and never reads the transfer row or the audit entry, so it is blind to D6. A reviewer would ask for an attribution assertion. It is the test gap of D6, not a second defect.

adjudicated.title: Overdraft test checks status only, misses persistence
adjudicated.note: True. The HTTP test asserts only the status of the overdraft route, never the body or a follow-up read, so it is blind to D4. Severity overstated: a test gap is not critical in itself; the defect it hides is.

adjudicated.title: canCover test bypasses store, misses lost overdraft
adjudicated.note: True. canCover is unit-tested with a hand-built object, so the store's stripping of overdraftCents is never exercised. The test gap of D4; same note on severity.

adjudicated.title: Literal JSON null body crashes the export route (500)
adjudicated.note: True. readJson returns JSON.parse's value as is, so a body of the literal text null makes body === null and `const { name } = body` throws, answered as a 500 instead of a 400. Introduced at this line by the PR; the same class exists on main for /transfers, which destructures its body too, so it is a fair medium rather than a new vulnerability.

adjudicated.title: Paged transfers test can't detect the off-by-one slice bug
adjudicated.note: True. The paging test uses three transfers, below PAGE_SIZE, so it passes with either slice end. The test gap of D1. Severity overstated for a test gap; the defect it hides is high.

adjudicated.title: Withdrawal never re-checks /summary after mutating totals
adjudicated.note: True. The HTTP test reads the summary after the deposit and only the balance after the withdrawal, so it is blind to D9. The test gap of D9.

adjudicated.title: Withdraw's closed-account 409 path is never tested
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. The statement is true, but the finding itself verified the code is correct; an untested correct path has no failure scenario, and the skill defines a finding as a defect with one. A coverage note, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Control regex misses C1 and Unicode line separators
adjudicated.note: True. The PR's own rule is one printable line; U+0080–U+009F are control characters and U+2028/U+2029 are line separators, and all pass the ASCII-only regex into storage and the CSV, where csvCell quotes only on comma, quote and newline. Severity overstated: medium, not high.

adjudicated.title: seed script still passes label, not name
adjudicated.note: True, and not planted: renaming openAccount's parameter from label to name also broke scripts/seed.mjs in this PR (it now throws 'label is required'), the same class of defect planted as D3 in PR #3. The author's accident, caught by the review. Severity: medium, as D3 is rated; critical overstates a seed script.

adjudicated.title: No test ever has ownerId differ from actor
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. True that nothing exercises the new ownerId override, but the override is correct and nothing fails; a coverage note on correct code, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Audit test's single transfer never exercises recipient-side or cross-account scoping
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. The route is correct (the finding does not claim otherwise); the test could be stronger, but an untested correct path has no failure scenario. A coverage note, not a defect.

adjudicated.title: Audit route scans the entire global collection, unpaginated
adjudicated.note: False as a finding. Every list in this service scans its in-memory collection; the audit route does what listAccounts and transfersFor do, on a JSON-file store that is whole in memory by design. No failure at any scale the service is built for; the response stays bounded to the account. A design remark, rated low by the review itself.

adjudicated.title: Accountant can close and export any account
adjudicated.note: True. The accountant test exercises the two read routes only, so it is blind to D5. The test gap of D5, worded as the defect itself; critical overstates a test gap.

adjudicated.title: POST /accounts crashes to 500 on JSON null body
adjudicated.note: True. Before this PR the route spread the body (`{ ...body, … }`), which tolerates null; the rewrite reads `body.label` directly, so a literal null JSON body throws and answers 500 instead of 400. Introduced at this line by the PR; the same class as the null-body finding on #7. Medium is fair.
